thread:
infra-alert-bot: 🚨 ALERT: multiple serving-runtime pods reporting CUDA illegal memory access on gpu-pool-7 (node=gw-7-12). OOM + container crash loop detected. Auto-retries hit rate-limit. See first ts=3103512345

infra-alert-bot: sample kernel log:
```
[ 1234.567890] NVRM: GPU 0: RmInitAdapter failed! (0x30)
[ 1234.567895] CudaKernel: illegal memory access at 0x7f9b3c000000 from tid 0x7f9b3c0
[ 1234.567900] oom-killer: task serving-runtime:3291 blocked for more than 120 seconds
```

sylvia: I'm oncall. I'm seeing ~18 pods in CrashLoopBackOff across 3 nodes in gpu-pool-7. Customer-facing traffic impacted for 2 mid-tier customers (embed-heavy). Marking sev2 for now.

omar: copy me @sylvia — starting triage. Does this look like the pagewalk/unaligned deviceaddr we've seen last month?

jin: @omar @sylvia probably related. Stack traces show device address translation faults during pagewalk. Could be a race in the new scatter-gather kernel path we rolled last week.

anya: heads-up from CS: customer "AtlasSearch" reports ~30% error rate on embedding calls since 08:02 UTC, complains timeouts. They're on dedicated capacity in us-east-1.

sylvia: Ok mitigation plan: 1) cordon affected nodes 2) scale up fallback CPU-backed pool 3) enable proxy retry/failover to quantized-cpu model 4) collect full dmesg and kube logs, attach to incident. Omar pls run cordon/drain. Jin pls validate model fallback. Nick will reach out to customers.

omar: running commands now:
```bash
kubectl cordon gw-7-12
kubectl drain gw-7-12 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --force
kubectl get pods -n serving -o wide | grep gw-7-12
```

deploy-bot: Deploy queued: rollback serving-runtime:v3.7.1 -> v3.6.9 (canary). Triggered by @omar. Canary target: 5 pods in us-east-1-f.

jin: quick check: the canary rollback removes the new kernel flag that enabled sg-pagewalk optimization. If we get stable canary we'll roll across gpu-pool-7. Also enabling runtime-level guard to disable async-kvcache prefetch which seems to trigger the sequence.

nick: pinging AtlasSearch (account rep on call). ETA to they acknowledged and are routing through fallback. They'll do a quick smoke.

anya: AtlasSearch confirms fallback reduces errors to <5% but latency up ~40ms. They're ok with auto-failover while you fix. Please include customer impact note in postmortem.

omar: Logs collected and uploaded: s3://redwood-incident-logs/3103512345/dmesg.tar.gz and kube-logs.tar.gz. Attaching kernel oops snippet to the thread.

sylvia: @eva-oncall can you take the next shift? I need to hand off once rollouts finish. Current state: canary rolled to 5 pods, no crashes in canary for 6 minutes. Rolling to remaining nodes paused until we see 10m stability.

eva-oncall: taking handoff. I've noted the rollback PR and will monitor. Checklist I'm using: health checks, backpressure queues, customer impact log, revert plan. Leaving cordon in place until full roll complete.

jin: root cause hypothesis for postmortem: a race between the sg-pagewalk refactor and the async prefetch path that causes stale pte usage, leading to illegal deviceaddr during pagewalk under memory pressure. Kernel/hw combination exposes it on certain firmware. Repro attempts in staging with stress-ng + large batch loads ongoing.

omar: follow-ups: 1) backfill kernel/firmware matrix for affected nodes 2) add guard in runtime to verify pte alignment 3) hotpatch candidate (userspace mitigation) PR #4021: disables prefetch windows for sg path.

sylvia: assigning owners: jin -> root cause + fix PR, omar -> rollout + operations runbook updates, nick/anya -> customer comms and impact doc. I'll write initial incident timeline.

infra-alert-bot: Incident updated: severity -> SEV2, status -> mitigation in progress, started_at -> 3103512345.

eva-oncall: note: metrics to track during handoff: pod restart rate, kernel oops count, embedding error rate for top-10 customers. Adding dashboard link: https://console.redwood/ops/d/incident-3103512345

nick: sending templated update to affected customers now. Message: "We've detected GPU node-level errors causing intermittent embedding failures. We've enabled fallback routing and rolled back the recent runtime flag. We're actively investigating and will follow up with a postmortem." :white_check_mark:

anya: I'll log customer acceptances and escalations. Also starting PS engagement for AtlasSearch if they want deeper SLA credits.

sylvia: good handoff. If canary stays clean for 10m we'll proceed to full rollout. Otherwise keep cordon/drain in place and escalate infra if hardware suspects. Thanks team. :pray:
